title: Adaptive Residual Modeling for Scenario Learning in Probabilistic Load Forecasting (abstract page)
note: arXiv v1 only, 2 Nov 2026, Wang, Liu, Zhang, Ma, Li, Yan; eess.SY; text licence CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. ARMSL: Stage I models weather response, load history, persistent residuals and innovations and draws joint active/reactive power scenarios for feeders; Stage II calibrates only extreme quantiles against a simple anchor forecast. No code or data link, no comments or journal ref on the page.

title: ARMSL abstract: headline numbers
note: Abstract numbers: on FeederBW the active-power 0.99-quantile pinball loss is 0.1932, 30.08% to 85.33% below three baselines, with exceedance 1.054% against nominal 1%. On Rolle, losses are 5.39% to 14.40% below the active-power-only anchor. Predicted vs observed feeder event rates correlate at 0.953 and 90.0% of feeder errors are within two percentage points.

title: ARMSL full text: data, horizon, inputs
note: FeederBW: P and Q for 200 German low-voltage feeders, 10-min means, two years, hourly weather fields; training ends 31 Mar 2024; 42,508 calibration and 567,908 evaluation cases; test dates and length not stated. Direct forecasts 10, 20, 30, 60 min ahead. Inputs limited to what is known at issue time; weather not said to be observed or forecast; no known-future weather described.

title: ARMSL full text: Rolle data
note: Rolle: 24 anonymised meters in a Swiss distribution grid with NWP, 10-min records, 13 Jan 2018 to 19 Jan 2019, cited by Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.3463137. Stage I trained before 1 Sep 2018, two months validation, 28 days to calibrate Stage II, then a 53-day test. Three seeds on Rolle only. How NWP enters the model is not stated explicitly.

title: ARMSL full text: method and baselines
note: Stage I: additive temperature/irradiance response, spline lag memory, sparse persistent shocks, Student-t innovations with state-dependent spread; 128 joint scenarios. Stage II: 112 parameters, CPU fit in 2.37 min; anchor is ridge autoregression for P, persistence for Q. Baselines WI-TFT, DiffLoad, OFDDT, said to share issue times, targets, causal inputs and cases. No foundation model.

title: ARMSL full text: results
note: FeederBW P 0.99-quantile pinball: ARMSL 0.1932 (units not stated), WI-TFT 0.2764, DiffLoad 0.4225, OFDDT 1.3170; cut vs WI-TFT 30.08% (site-clustered 95% CI 27.40 to 32.50), vs DiffLoad 54.27%, vs OFDDT 85.33%. Stage I vs DiffLoad: energy score -11.02%, variogram -37.46%; vs OFDDT -23.58%, -28.49%. Rolle cut vs P-only anchor at 10/20/30/60 min: 5.39, 5.83, 6.29, 14.40%.

title: ARMSL full text: availability and limitations
note: No code, weights or repository statement; FeederBW is cited to a 2026 Scientific Data paper without a URL. No pre-registration mentioned. No seeds for FeederBW (bootstrap intervals only). Authors' limits: Rolle needs 28 days of local calibration, transfer to new regions untested, only extreme marginal endpoints calibrated, end-to-end training and inference cost not measured.

title: Search: ARMSL paper title plus code github (no repository found)
note: Search for the paper title with 'ARMSL code github' found nothing: no official repository. Hits were other papers' repositories; an aggregator page showed unrelated code links next to the ARMSL abstract, none attributable to this paper.

title: Search: ARMSL FeederBW replication or reproduction or implementation (no replication found)
note: Search found no third-party rerun or implementation of ARMSL. Results were the arXiv paper itself and other studies on the same FeederBW feeders (foundation-model benchmarks for low-voltage load) that do not test ARMSL. A search summary called FeederBW public; the data record itself was not opened.
